{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks.}}}}

{{GHGheb|text=אָב|translate=father}}; the {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִי}}, like {{GHGheb|text=אֲחִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=בְּנִי}} (which occurs once), belongs to the connective forms discussed in {{GHGpar|90|k}}, which serve as the model for the ''Ḥireq compaginis''. However, {{GHGheb|text=אַב}} also occurs in compound proper names, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַבְשָׁלוֹם}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִֽישָׁלוֹם}}, &c.; also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=4 f.}} {{GHGheb|text=אַב־הֲמוֹן}} for the purpose of explaining the name {{GHGheb|text=אב[ר]הם}}. On the plur. {{GHGheb|text=אָבוֹת}} see {{GHGpar|87|p}}.

{{GHGheb|text=אָח|translate=brother}}. The plur. {{GHGterm|absol.}} {{GHGheb|text=אַחִים}} has ''Dageš forte implicitum'' ({{GHGpar|22|c}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָיו}} stands for {{GHGheb|text=אַחָיו}} according to the phonetic law stated in {{GHGpar|27|q}}, and so also {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָֽי}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} for {{GHGheb|text=אַחָֽי}}. The sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ח}} merely serves to keep the preceding {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} short, as in {{GHGheb|text=גְּמַלִּים}}, &c. ({{GHGpar|93|ee}}).

{{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד|translate=one}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אַחָד}}, likewise with ''Dageš forte implicitum'', {{GHGpar|22|c}}, cf. {{GHGpar|27|q}}), {{GHGterm|constr.}} and otherwise in close connexion, {{GHGheb|text=אַחַד}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=12}},<section end=par96 /><noinclude>
